goals.en:
Upon the successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

Knowledge and understanding:
• Understand basic concepts such as energy needs; energy transition; energy conversion, transmission and storage; systems analysis; electric grids; specific energy technologies (Biofuel, Sun, Wind).
• Develop an overview of the various approaches to sustainable energy production
• Describe the driving forces behind an energy transition as well as its central prerequisites and challenges

Applying knowledge and understanding:
• Connect current developments in technology and policy to transition theory
• Assess claims to sustainability in the context of energy systems
• Address the concept of sustainability as it pertains to energy

Making judgements:
• Reflect on the individuals' and society’s role in energy transition
• Understand how different contexts fundamentally shape energy systems and the dynamics of transition
• Reflect on the ethical concerns related to energy transition
• Gather information about energy and reflect on its relevance and reliability

Communication:
• Explain the need for an interdisciplinary approach to sustainable energy transition
• Communicate about sources of uncertainty and about relevant context of data production

Learning skills:
• Evaluate, use and contextualise complex data at different scales
• Present work orally, in writing and visually while using the basic skills of scientific analysis
• Find, critically evaluate, use, and contextualise complex data at different scales (regional, national, global)
• Understand different types of uncertainty or incompleteness of scientific dataurrent developments in technology and policy to transition theory.

description.en:
This course will help students understand the dynamics of energy transition, including issues of climate change, development and sustainability. It will address the necessary structural changes in our energy systems and conceptions of energy. Students will gain insight into different models of transition and the connections between technologies, resources, governance, economics, behaviour and the culture of energy at different scales.

The course will address the following themes: energy needs; energy transition; energy and sustainability issues; energy conversion, transmission and storage; systems analysis; electric grids; specific energy technologies (Geothermal, Sun, Wind).

This course is designed to provide you with the methods, tools and perspectives to understand, critique, and ultimately influence the management of technical, economic, and policy choices regarding the options for energy generation and use.

Understanding energy systems requires an interdisciplinary approach that embodies the scientific, technical, economic, social, political and environmental opportunities and impacts of our energy system. Thus, this course will be a highly interdisciplinary experience, combining analytic tools, social, economic, historical and policy analysis from a variety of disciplines.

In particular, the course will address the Sustainable Development Goal 7: Affordable and Clean Energy.

Several elements in this course build on the basics learned in the foundations course Earth System, including:
- Systems thinking, feedback loops, climate dynamics and the carbon cycle.
- Impact of emissions from fossil fuel on climate in Earth System: this gives a foundation for understanding urgency of energy transition in this course
- Energy balance on Earth and Carbon Cycle covered in Earth System: provides a basis for understanding of all energy on Earth as originating with solar radiation
- Thinking on a global scale learned in Earth System is important cognitive framework to think about energy transition

This course further connects to other foundations courses:
- Complementary to Applied Social Psychology and to Global Health; in this course, ‘practice theory’ approach to behavioural change
- Relation to Introduction to Economics: Penalties for polluters; external costs to production

This course further develops skills and knowledge in understanding and using key concepts in the programme GRL:
- Sustainability in its different aspects and where these different understandings of sustainability originate
- The close connection of social, economic, political and technological dimensions
- The role of data in formulating and monitoring policy
- Energy in the context of sustainable development goals
- Dynamics of technological innovation for sustainability
